entities.summary: William IV of Egmont was a prominent Lord of Egmont, IJsselstein, Schoonderwoerd, and Haastrecht, and as Stadtholder of Guelders, he played a crucial role in the politics of the region. His significance lies in his ability to navigate the complexities of the Holy Roman Empire and his efforts to maintain the power and influence of the Dutch provinces. The legacy of William IV of Egmont can be seen in the continued importance of the Dutch nobility and the regional politics of the Low Countries. He was succeeded by his son, who continued to shape the political landscape of the region. William IV of Egmont's legacy is a testament to the enduring impact of medieval European politics on the modern world. The Egmont family's influence can still be felt in the region's cultural heritage and historical landmarks.
